s.dp: Attitudes and Emotions › Worry, Anxiety, Distress, Peace
s.d: a feeling of apprehension or distress in view of possible danger or misfortune
s.c: For μέριμνα as part of an idiom in ⟦1 Peter 5:7|1 Peter 5:7⟧, see LN 25.250.|The term μέριμνα may refer to either unnecessary worry or legitimate concern. The equivalent of ‘worry’ may be expressed in some languages in an idiomatic manner, for example, ‘to be killed by one’s mind’ or ‘to be pained by thinking.’

s.dp: Attitudes and Emotions › Worry, Anxiety, Distress, Peace
s.d: (an idiom, literally: to cast cares upon) to stop worrying and to put one’s trust in someone
s.g: to put one’s cares upon; to leave one’s worries to
s.c: For another explanation of this expression in ⟦1 Peter 5:7|1 Peter 5:7⟧, taking only ἐπιρίπτω ἐπί as an idiom, see LN 90.18.

s.dp: Attitudes and Emotions › Worry, Anxiety, Distress, Peace
s.d: (derivative of {L:μέριμνα<SDBG:μέριμνα:000000>} ‘worry,’ {D:25.224}) to have an anxious concern, based on apprehension about possible danger or misfortune
s.g: to be worried about; to be anxious about

s.d: part or portion, with the possible implication of a division or significant distinction

s.dp: Geographical Objects and Features › Governmental Administrative Areas
s.d: an administrative district
s.c: In ⟦Acts 16:12|Acts 16:12⟧ (the only occurrence of μερίς in the NT) the Greek New Testament published by the United Bible Societies has adopted a conjectural emendation, since the more traditional text, πρώτη τῆς μερίδος, literally ‘first of the district,’ is not only misleading in meaning but does not reflect the historical fact that Philippi was a city in one of the four districts of Macedonia but was not a capital city.

s.d: the point at which parts divide or meet
s.g: the point of division; the point of meeting

s.d: to distribute objects to a series of persons
s.g: to distribute; to give to each in turn; distribution

s.d: (derivative of {L:μερίζω<SDBG:μερίζω:000000>}[a] ‘to divide,’ {D:63.23}) one who divides
a part in contrast with a whole
an area at the side of an object

s.dp: Geographical Objects and Features › Sociopolitical Areas
s.d: region or regions of the earth, normally in relation to some ethnic group or geographical center, but not necessarily constituting a unit of governmental administration{N:001}
s.g: region; territory; land; district (though this might imply too precisely a governmental area)
s.c: The meanings of γῆ, χώρα, κλίμαὅριον, and μέρος are not to be regarded as completely synonymous, but in certain of their NT usages they are largely overlapping in reference.

s.dp: Groups and Classes of Persons and Members of Such Groups and Classes › General
s.d: a group of people having specific membership and forming a part of a larger constituency
s.c: In the NT μέρος occurs only in the expression μέρος τῶν Φαρισαίων the party of the Pharisees, and though the Pharisees constituted a socio-religious group, the use of μέρος does not focus upon this socio-religious aspect of the Pharisees relationship to the Jewish nation as a whole, but merely upon their identity as a part of a larger constituency. The expression the party of the Pharisees may be rendered in some languages as the group to which the Pharisees belonged or those who were counted as Pharisees or the division called Pharisees. In selecting a word for party or group, it is important to avoid a term which would be essentially political in meaning. If there is no general term for party, it may be necessary to use one with a socio-religious denotation, since that would be the most accurate way of identifying the Pharisees in their relationship to other distinctive groups in the Jewish nation.

s.dp: Possess, Transfer, Exchange › Earn, Gain, Do Business
s.d: a particular kind of business activity or occupation
a degree which is only part of some totality{N:002}
s.g: partially; to some degree; part; partly

s.d: (idioms, literally: from a part) the state of being part of something
s.g: being part of; as a part of; in part; partially

s.dp: Time › Duration of Time without Reference to Points or Units of Time: Time, Spend Time, Always, Eternal, Old, Immediately, Young
s.d: (an idiom, literally: from a part) pertaining to a relatively short period of time, with emphasis upon the temporary nature of the event or state
s.g: not long; temporary; for a little while; for a while

s.dp: Time › A Point of Time with Reference to Units of Time: Daybreak, Midday, Midnight, Late
s.d: the midpoint of a day
s.c: In a number of languages μεσημβρία may be rendered as ‘when the sun is high’ or ‘when the sun is above one’s head’ or ‘just as the sun starts down.’ For another interpretation of μεσημβρία in ⟦Acts 8:26|Acts 8:26⟧, see LN 82.4.

s.dp: Spacial Orientations › North, South, East, West
s.c: It is also possible to interpret κατὰ μεσημβρίαν in ⟦Acts 8:26|Acts 8:26⟧ as meaning ‘about noon,’ since μεσημβρία is a normal expression for ‘midday’ or ‘noon’ (see LN 67.74). See also the discussion at LN 82.3.

s.dp: Hold a View, Believe, Trust › Agree, Consent
s.d: to bring about a mutually accepted agreement between two or more parties, with the probable additional component of making something certain
s.g: to bring about an agreement; to cause an agreement
s.c: Since one who was a μεσίτης (LN 31.22) often acted as one who provided the surety or guarantee of an agreement or arrangement, there is a significant component of certainty involved in μεσιτεύω. Hence, one may understand this as implying not only the agreement but the guarantee of its validity.

s.dp: Hold a View, Believe, Trust › Agree, Consent
s.d: (derivative of {L:μεσιτεύω<SDBG:μεσιτεύω:000000>} ‘to bring about an agreement,’ {D:31.21}) one who causes or helps parties to come to an agreement, with the implication of guaranteeing the certainty of the arrangement
a person who acts as a mediator in bringing about reconciliation{N:001}
s.c: A mediator may be spoken of in a number of different ways, often idiomatically, for example, ‘one who stands in the middle,’ ‘one who speaks to both,’ ‘one who cuts palavers,’ or ‘one who causes arguments to cease.’ It is also possible, however, to regard μεσίτης as being related to the process of causing agreement between the parties in question. For this aspect of the meaning of μεσίτης, see LN 31.22.

s.dp: Time › A Point of Time with Reference to Units of Time: Daybreak, Midday, Midnight, Late
s.d: the midpoint of the night
s.c: In some languages μεσονύκτιον may be rendered as ‘when the night is half over’ or ‘when the night is cut in half.’

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Places
s.d: the valley of the Euphrates and Tigris rivers

s.dp: Spacial Positions › Among, Between, In, Inside
s.d: a position within an area determined by other objects and distributed among such objects{N:001}

s.dp: Spacial Positions › Among, Between, In, Inside
s.d: a position in the middle of an area (either an object in the midst of other objects or an area in the middle of a larger area){N:003}
s.g: in the middle; in the midst

s.d: a wall or fence which separates one area from another
s.c: In the NT μεσότοιχον is used figuratively in reference to the partition in the Temple in Jerusalem, which set off the court of the Gentiles from the rest of the Temple area.|Such a ‘dividing wall’ may be rendered as ‘barrier’ or ‘fence which separates.’

s.dp: Geographical Objects and Features › Regions Above the Earth
s.d: a point or region of the sky directly above the earth
s.g: high in the sky; midpoint in the sky; directly overhead; straight above in the sky

s.dp: Time › Duration of Time with Reference to Some Unit of Time: During, In, While, Throughout
s.d: to be in the middle of a period of time
s.g: to be in the middle of; to have something half over

s.d: (literally: one who has been anointed) in the NT, titles for Jesus as the Messiah, but in many contexts, and especially without an article, {L:Χριστός<SDBG:Χριστός:000000>} becomes a part of the name of Jesus; see {D:93.387})
s.c: In a number of languages Χριστός (or Μεσσίας) as a reference to the Messiah occurs in a transliterated form based either on Χριστός in Greek or on Messiah in Hebrew. However, in some languages an attempt is made to represent the significance of the terms Χριστός and Μεσσίας by translating ‘God’s appointed one’ or ‘God’s specially chosen one’ or ‘the expected one,’ in the sense of one to whom everyone was looking for help and deliverance.

s.d: pertaining to a quantity that fills a space beyond expectations or appropriateness
a degree of completeness, with the implication of abundance
s.c: In a number of languages it is simply not possible to speak of a person being ‘full of’ some quality or ‘full of’ some type of activity. Accordingly, one must often restructure the semantic relationships so as to indicate that one is ‘completely’ of a certain nature or ‘entirely’ engaged in some activity. In fact, in some languages this may be expressed negatively in the case of ⟦Matthew 23:28|Matthew 23:28⟧ as ‘within there is nothing but hypocrisy and lawlessness.’ In the case of ⟦James 3:17|James 3:17⟧ one can often express the meaning in terms of habitual activity, for example, ‘always merciful and doing good things.’

s.d: pertaining to being extensively engaged in some activity or attitude
s.g: to be full of; to be constantly engaged in

s.d: (derivative of {L:μεστός<SDBG:μεστός:000000>}[a] ‘very full,’ {D:59.39}) to cause a space to be exceptionally full
s.g: to fill; to cause to bulge
s.c: In many instances one cannot speak of persons being ‘full of new wine.’ It is, however, possible in ⟦Acts 2:13|Acts 2:13⟧ to say ‘they have drunk a great deal of new wine.’

s.d: a marker of an associative relation, usually with the implication of being in the company of{N:001}
s.g: with; in the company of; together with

s.d: a marker of association, involving instruments relevant to an event
a marker of a relation in which one thing is combined with another
s.c: This expression in ⟦Luke 13:1|Luke 13:1⟧ must be understood in a figurative sense, for it refers to the act of Pilate killing the people while they were sacrificing.|In some languages this expression in ⟦Ephesians 6:23|Ephesians 6:23⟧ can only be expressed as ‘love and trust at the same time.’ |In ⟦1 Timothy 2:15|1 Timothy 2:15⟧ modesty is in a combinative relation with faith, love, and holiness and not merely with holiness. In languages in which such expressions are normally translated by verbs, one may render the final clause of ⟦1 Timothy 2:15|1 Timothy 2:15⟧ as ‘if she continues to trust and love and to be holy while at the same time showing modesty.’

s.d: a marker of circumstances which contribute significantly to the context of the principal event{N:002}
a marker of the experiencer of an event, with the added implication of association
(with the genitive) a marker of opposition and conflict, implying interaction

s.dp: Time › A Point of Time with Reference to Other Points of Time: Before, Long Ago, Now, At the Same Time, When, About, After
s.d: a marker of a point of time closely associated with a prior point of time
s.c: In a number of languages there is no convenient preposition-like word such as ‘after,’ but one can render the expression in ⟦John 3:22|John 3:22⟧ as ‘these things happened, and then Jesus and his disciples went to the province of Judea.’

s.dp: Spacial Positions › Among, Between, In, Inside
s.d: a position within an area determined by other objects and distributed among such objects{N:004}

s.dp: Spacial Positions › Beyond, On the Other Side Of
s.d: (with the genitive) a position farther away and behind some object
a marker of association in which one party acts or exists for the benefit of another
s.g: with; on the same side as
s.c: In ⟦Matthew 12:30|Matthew 12:30⟧ there is an implied event.

s.d: a marker of means, with the probable additional implication of attendant circumstance (see {L:μετά<SDBG:μετά:000003>}[d] ‘with,’ {D:89.79})
s.c: In ⟦Acts 2:28|Acts 2:28⟧ πρόσωπον is a figurative designation for the presence of a person (see LN 85.26).

s.d: to effect a change of location in space, with the implication that the two locations are significantly different
s.g: to move from one place to another; to change one’s location; to depart; departure

s.dp: Be, Become, Exist, Happen › Change of State

s.dp: Hold a View, Believe, Trust › Change an Opinion Concerning Truth
s.d: to change one’s thinking about something
s.g: to change one’s mind; to alter an opinion
s.c: In ⟦Acts 28:6|Acts 28:6⟧ μεταβάλλομαι may often be expressed as ‘to no longer think as they did’ or ‘to think differently now.’

s.d: to cause to move from one place to another by bringing or leading
s.g: to direct; to steer; to guide

s.d: to share with someone else what one has
to effect a change of location in space, with the implication that the two locations are significantly different
s.g: to move from one place to another; to change one’s location; to depart; departure
s.c: In view of the specific reference of μετάθεσις in ⟦Hebrews 11:5|Hebrews 11:5⟧, it is possible to speak of ‘being taken up,’ but the meaning is clearly a significant change of location from one place to another, that is to say, from earth to heaven.

s.dp: Be, Become, Exist, Happen › Change of State
s.d: a change from one state to another

s.dp: Linear Movement › Leave, Depart, Flee, Escape, Send
s.d: to move away from a reference point, perhaps more definitively than in the case of {L:πορεύομαι<SDBG:πορεύομαι:000002>}[c] and {L:ἄγω<SDBG:ἄγω:000002>}[c] ({D:15.34})
s.g: to go; to go away from; to depart; to leave

s.d: to summon someone, with considerable insistence and authority
s.g: to summon; to tell to come

s.d: to cause a state to cease, with the implication of force
s.g: to cause to cease; to be shaken from

s.d: to receive as one’s share in or as one’s part of
s.g: to receive a share in; to have a share of

s.d: to experience some event or state, often with the implication of something negatively valued{N:001}
to receive as one’s share in or as one’s part of
s.g: to receive a share in; to have a share of
s.c: In ⟦1 Timothy 4:3|1 Timothy 4:3⟧ the reference of μετάλημψιν is to the activity of eating, and therefore one may translate as ‘which God created for people to eat,’ but one should not mistake the reference of μετάλημψιν for the meaning of the term.

s.d: to exchange one thing for another{N:001}
s.c: In rendering μεταλλάσσω in ⟦Romans 1:25|Romans 1:25⟧ it is essential to avoid anything which might mean ‘to change something into.’ It is the substitution of one thing for another; hence, ‘exchange’ rather than ‘change’ is the correct gloss.

s.d: to cease one activity and to start something else in exchange
s.g: to cease and to start; to exchange

s.d: to feel regret as the result of what one has done
s.g: to regret; to feel sad about; to feel sorry because of

s.dp: Hold a View, Believe, Trust › Change an Opinion Concerning Truth
s.d: to change one’s mind about something, with the probable implication of regret
s.g: to change one’s mind; to think differently

s.dp: Be, Become, Exist, Happen › Change of State
s.d: to change the essential form or nature of something
s.g: to become; to change; to be changed into; to be transformed
s.c: In a number of languages the equivalent of μεταμορφόομαι in ⟦Romans 12:2|Romans 12:2⟧ may be ‘become completely different’ or ‘become different from what you are.’

s.dp: Nature, Class, Example › Appearance as an Outward Manifestation of Form
s.d: to take on a different physical form or appearance
s.c: In some instances it may be more appropriate to render this expression in ⟦Mark 9:2|Mark 9:2⟧ as ‘as they watched, he appeared different.’

s.dp: Behavior and Related States › Change Behavior
s.d: to change one’s way of life as the result of a complete change of thought and attitude with regard to sin and righteousness{N:001}
s.g: to repent; to change one’s way; repentance
s.c: Though in English a focal component of repent is the sorrow or contrition that a person experiences because of sin, the emphasis in μετανοέω and μετάνοια seems to be more specifically the total change, both in thought and behavior, with respect to how one should both think and act. Whether the focus is upon attitude or behavior varies somewhat in different contexts. Compare, for example, ⟦Luke 3:8|Luke 3:8⟧, ⟦Hebrews 6:1|Hebrews 6:1⟧, and ⟦Acts 26:20|Acts 26:20⟧.

s.dp: Behavior and Related States › Change Behavior
s.d: to change one’s way of life as the result of a complete change of thought and attitude with regard to sin and righteousness{N:001}
s.g: to repent; to change one’s way; repentance
s.c: Though in English a focal component of repent is the sorrow or contrition that a person experiences because of sin, the emphasis in μετανοέω and μετάνοια seems to be more specificaly the total change, both in thought and behavior, with respect to how one should both think and act. Whether the focus is upon attitude or behavior varies somewhat in different contexts. Compare, for example, ⟦Luke 3:8|Luke 3:8⟧, ⟦Hebrews 6:1|Hebrews 6:1⟧, and ⟦Acts 26:20|Acts 26:20⟧.

s.dp: Spacial Positions › Among, Between, In, Inside
s.d: a position defined by the location of two objects, one on each side
a marker of an exclusive association

s.dp: Time › A Point of Time with Reference to Other Points of Time: Before, Long Ago, Now, At the Same Time, When, About, After
s.d: a point of time which is subsequent in order to a previous point of time

s.dp: Linear Movement › Leave, Depart, Flee, Escape, Send
s.d: to send someone to obtain something or someone
s.c: In some languages it may be important to make somewhat more explicit some of the implied events or relationships in this phrase in ⟦Acts 10:5|Acts 10:5⟧, for example, ‘ask a certain Simon called Peter to come’ or ‘deliver a message to a certain Simon called Peter asking him to come.’

s.dp: Be, Become, Exist, Happen › Change of State
s.d: to cause a change of state, with emphasis upon the difference in the resulting state{N:001}
s.g: to change to; to turn into; to cause to be different from; to transform

s.dp: Be, Become, Exist, Happen › Change of State
s.d: to cause a change of state, with emphasis upon the difference in the resulting state{N:001}
s.g: to change to; to turn into; to cause to be different from; to transform

s.dp: Nature, Class, Example › Appearance as an Outward Manifestation of Form
s.d: to cause a change in the form of something
s.g: to change; to change from one form into another

s.d: to relate something to something else on the basis of certain correspondences
s.g: to apply to; to regard as applicable to

s.d: to effect a change of location in space, with the implication that the two locations are significantly different
s.g: to move from one place to another; to change one’s location; to depart; departure

s.dp: Be, Become, Exist, Happen › Change of State
s.d: to cause a change of state, with emphasis upon the difference in the resulting state{N:001}
s.g: to change to; to turn into; to cause to be different from; to transform

s.d: (an idiom, literally: to change from) to abandon an association
s.g: to turn away from; to abandon one’s loyalty to

s.dp: Time › A Point of Time with Reference to Other Points of Time: Before, Long Ago, Now, At the Same Time, When, About, After
s.d: a point of time following another point{N:001}

s.dp: Possess, Transfer, Exchange › Have, Possess, Property, Owner
s.d: to share in the possession of something
s.g: to share in; to have a share of

s.dp: Physiological Processes and States › Eat, Drink
s.d: (normally occurring together with a term specifying the particular food in question, but also occurring absolutely in contexts relating to food; μετέχω[b] is probably more formal than {L:ἐσθίω<SDBG:ἐσθίω:000000>}[a], {D:23.1}) to partake of or to consume food, whether solid or liquid{N:001}
s.g: to eat; to eat food; to drink
s.c: In contexts in which μετέχω occurs, it may be important to select a term for the eating which will go specifically with the type of food in question. For various types of distinctions made in terms for eating, see the discussion at LN 23.1 and its footnote.

s.dp: Association › Belong To, Be Included in the Membership of, Be Excluded From
s.d: to be included in the membership of a group
s.c: In order to express the meaning of ‘belonged to a different tribe,’ it may be necessary to say ‘he had a different tribe name’ or ‘his tribe was different’ or ‘he was counted as a member of another tribe.’

s.dp: Association › Belong To, Be Included in the Membership of, Be Excluded From
s.d: (an idiom, literally: to share in a table) to belong to a particular religious group as evidenced by ceremonial eating{N:002}
s.g: to belong to (a religious group); to eat at the table of

s.dp: Attitudes and Emotions › Worry, Anxiety, Distress, Peace
s.d: to be very concerned about, with the implication of placing too much value upon something
s.g: to be anxious about; to be concerned about

s.d: act of causing someone to change a place of habitation
to cause someone to change a place of habitation
s.g: to resettle; to move to another place; to deport; deportation

s.d: a relationship involving shared purposes and activity
s.c: In ⟦2 Corinthians 6:14|2 Corinthians 6:14⟧ δικαιοσύνη and ἀνομία refer to ‘those who do right’ and ‘those who do wrong.’ In fact, in a number of languages one can only translate this expression in ⟦2 Corinthians 6:14|2 Corinthians 6:14⟧ as ‘how can a person who does right and one who does wrong join in a partnership?’ or ‘how can one who does right and one who does wrong work together?’ In this same verse κοινωνία (see LN 34.5) has a meaning closely corresponding to μετοχή, and similarly φῶς and σκότος refer respectively to ‘those who live in the light’ and ‘those who live in darkness,’ paralleling closely the distinction between δικαιοσύνη and ἀνομία.

s.d: one who shares with someone else as an associate in an enterprise or undertaking
to determine the measurement of something
s.c: In some languages one may best translate this expression in ⟦Revelation 21:16|Revelation 21:16⟧ as ‘the angel learned how big the city was’ or, as in other languages, ‘the angel walked the size of the city.’

s.d: to give a measured portion to someone
s.c: It is possible to interpret this expression in ⟦Mark 4:24|Mark 4:24⟧ (and also in ⟦Matthew 7:2|Matthew 7:2⟧) as used in a more figurative sense, for example, ‘he will deal with you in the manner that you deal with others.’

s.dp: Spacial Dimensions › Specific Measures of Volume
s.d: a liquid measure of about nine gallons or forty liters

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Gentleness, Mildness
s.d: to be gentle in one’s attitude toward someone
s.g: to deal gently with; to be gently disposed toward

s.d: a moderate degree of some activity or state
s.c: In ⟦Acts 20:12|Acts 20:12⟧ the phrase οὐ μετρίως, literally ‘not to a moderate degree,’ is equivalent to a strong positive statement, namely, ‘greatly’ or ‘to a great extent.’

s.d: a unit of measurement, either of length or volume
s.c: Some languages do not have a generic term for ‘measure,’ but they may express the concept by a phrase meaning ‘how one knows how big something is’ or ‘… how long something is.’ In other words, it is necessary to use expressions involving specific dimensions.

s.d: (an idiom, literally: from measure) a scalar point marking considerable limitation in the extent of some activity
s.c: In a number of languages this expression in ⟦John 3:34|John 3:34⟧ may be appropriately rendered as ‘he doesn’t hold back at all when he gives the Spirit’ or ‘he gives the Spirit in an abundant way.’

s.dp: Body, Body Parts, and Body Products › Parts of the Body
s.d: the front part of the head above the eyes
s.c: Though in most languages there is a specific term to designate the forehead, it may be necessary in some instances to speak of ‘the upper face’ or ‘the face above the eyes.’

s.dp: Time › Duration of Time with Reference to Some Point of Time: Until, Delay, Still, From
s.d: the continuous extent of time up to a point{N:001}
s.g: until; to; at last; at length
s.c: The phrase εἰ μὴ ὅταν is often translated as ‘until’ (for example, μηδενὶ ἅ εἶδον διηγήσωνταιεἰ μὴ ὅταν ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐκ νεκρῶν ἀναστῇ ‘not to tell anybody what they have seen until the Son of Man has risen from death’ ⟦Mark 9:9|Mark 9:9⟧), but this phrase may be analyzed as meaning ‘if it is not when,’ an expression which is semantically equivalent to ‘until.’

s.dp: Spacial Extensions › Extension To a Goal
s.d: extension up to or as far as a goal{N:002}
s.g: to; up to; as far as

s.dp: Degree › Up To, As Much As, To the Degree That [Marked Extent of Degree]
s.d: a degree extending to a particular point as marked by the context

s.dp: Know › Not Able To Be Known, Secret
s.d: (an idiom, probably an adage or traditional saying, literally: do not let your left hand know what your right hand is doing) an admonition to do something without letting people know about it
s.g: to do something secretly; to do something without letting the public know
s.c: It is rare that one can preserve this idiom, since in its literal form it may seem absurd. For many English-speaking people the meaning has already been twisted by common usage to mean ‘be sure to not let anyone know if you are performing something that is shady or illegal.’ Today’s English Version attempts to represent something of the impact of this idiom by translating “do it in such a way that even your closest friend will not know about it.”

s.c: Though in English one may readily say ‘tell no one’ or ‘take nothing,’ in a number of languages the negation must be related to the verb and not to a pronominal object. Accordingly, it may be necessary to translate as ‘do not tell anyone’ or ‘do not take anything.’

s.dp: Kinship Terms › Kinship Relations Involving Successive Generations
s.d: one’s biological or adoptive female parent
s.c: μήτηρ is sometimes used figuratively to refer to persons who are not biological parents but who are in some respects closely associated with the reference person: μήτηρ μου καὶ ἀδελφοί μου οὗτοί εἰσιν οἱ τὸν λόγον τοῦ θεοῦ ἀκούοντες καὶ ποιοῦντες ‘my mother and my brothers are those who hear God’s word and act accordingly’ ⟦Luke 8:21|Luke 8:21⟧. s.dp: Affirmation, Negation › Markers for a Negative Response to Questions
s.d: a marker of a somewhat more emphatic negative response
s.c: Some persons have argued that the occurrence of μήτι in ⟦John 4:29|John 4:29⟧ is contradictory, since it would appear from the context that the individuals posing the question regarded Jesus as a possible Messiah. On the other hand, asking the question in this form would have certainly fit the circumstances in which there was strong opposition to anyone claiming that Jesus was the Messiah. This form of the question would have avoided an overt commitment, while at the same time indicating peoples evident interest and concern.

s.d: a marker of emphasis, involving some degree of contrast and/or comparison

s.dp: Body, Body Parts, and Body Products › Parts of the Body
s.d: the uterus
s.c: For the total expression as an idiom, see LN 10.45. Rarely can one translate literally ⟦Luke 2:23|Luke 2:23⟧ as ‘every male that opens the womb,’ since this is likely to refer to an adult male who first has sexual intercourse with a woman. The reference in ⟦Luke 2:23|Luke 2:23⟧ is, of course, to the first male child which is born to a woman, and therefore an appropriate equivalent in many languages is ‘a woman’s first baby if it is a boy.’
